name: Tessek Yuzu-Honey Hard Candy
description: Hand-pulled hard candies in yuzu-honey flavor, made in small batches with real honey — a genuine ingredient that drives the price above mass-market alternatives. The translucent amber pieces are visually distinctive.
flavor_profile: Bright yuzu citrus zest and floral bitterness balanced by genuine honey sweetness; the candy is glassy and clear, not cloudy; dissolves cleanly with no artificial aftertaste
cultural_context: The 'real honey' call-out on the tin is a deliberate status signal — Tessek buyers want people to know they're eating something real. The tins are reusable and often kept as small containers after the candy is gone. A Tessek tin on someone's desk in a Tier 3 office means something.
story_hooks: Tessek's honey supplier — a vertical apiary operation in the upper Spire greenhouse levels — has just been bought out; the new owner is diluting the product
A Tessek tin found at a crime scene is the only luxury item present, suggesting the victim or perpetrator was either Tier 3-4 or was given the candy by someone who is
Someone is refilling Tessek tins with a cheaper product and reselling them at full price through secondary markets — and the forgeries are very good
